To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the growth of the d-biotin producer Serratia maracescens is inhibited by the introduction into it of its own plasmid-borne biotin operons.

the growth of the biotin-producing strain of the bacterium Serratia marce- scens (SB412), which is inhibited by the introduction into it of pLGM 412, a low- copy-number plasmid carrying the complete bio operon derived from the SB412, is caused by the overexpression of the biot- in synthase gene, and that the plasmid is genetically unstable.
the biotin operons of a biotin-overproducing S. marcescens strain are genetically unstable in the presence of a wild-type strain, which is caused by a high expression of the bio genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the genetic instability of the bio operon plasmids in the bio-overproducing strain of S. marcescens and the instability is considered to be due to a high expression of the bioB gene product in the host cell.
the growth inhibition of SB412 by the bio operon plasmids and the instability of the bio operon in SB412.
the instability and the high expression of the bio operon in SB412 carrying pLMG412.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high expression level of biotin synthetase causes the growth inhibition, and this growth inhibition is responsible for the genetic instability of the mutated plasmids.
the bio operon is unstable and the instability is due to the high expression of the bioB gene product, which is toxic to SB412.

the high expression and the resultant high production of d-biotin in the SB412 strain causes growth inhibition by some unknown mechanism(s) and that the growth inhibition can be relieved by mutations in the bioB gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the high expression levels of the bio genes are toxic to the cell, and the cell is protected from the toxicity by genetic instability of the bio operon.
the bioB gene expression in the host is toxic to the host.
the high expression levels of bioB gene in the host SB412 cause the growth inhibition and genetic instability of the bio plasmid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth inhibition of the bioB-overproducing strain was relieved by the mutation in the bioB gene.
the biotin operons of the bioB mutant strains of S. marcescens are genetically unstable.
the high expression level of the biotin biosynthesis gene(s) is responsible for the instability of pLGM4 12 in SB412.
